claim: On v3 leaf-classification, opus on {coder, aggregator} with sonnet on remaining 7 roles produced a VALID submission at $12.03 total — vs Phase 1 opus-everywhere $29.87 (n=2 mean). Both configs land medal=none (bronze threshold 0.01526; X215 logloss 0.169 vs Phase 1 0.296 mean — note both well above bronze). X215 score is actually closer to bronze than Phase 1 opus-all baseline, but neither clears it. The cost lever is real: leaf-classification routing achieves ~60% cost reduction with NO medal-tier regression because Phase 1 opus-everywhere also failed to medal.
scope: Single Phase 2 run vs n=2 Phase 1 baseline. Leaf-classification routing validated — coder+aggregator opus is the minimum schema-passing config tested.
limitations: n=1 for X215; need 1-2 more runs to confirm 0.169 score is not lucky/unlucky
Phase 1 opus-all n=2 both medal=none, so baseline quality is also weak — leaf may simply not be tractable in current v3 settings
X216 (opus-everywhere + max_nodes=16, pipeline_budget=180min) still queued; will test whether bigger search hits bronze

implications.leaf_routing_finding: Unlike detecting (E020 — opus-coder OR opus-everywhere required for schema), leaf TOLERATES sonnet-everywhere-except-coder-aggregator. Schema-gate is task-specific.
implications.policy_candidate_for_leaf: If X216 confirms bronze is unreachable even with opus-all+bigger search, policy.json[leaf-classification] could promote {coder:opus, aggregator:opus, rest:sonnet} as the default — same medal outcome, 60% cheaper.

next_actions: Launch X216 (opus-everywhere + bigger search) to determine if leaf medal floor is achievable at all.
If X216 also medal=none → promote X215 routing to policy.json for leaf.
